source: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)
extraction_note: Extracted directly from a chart export the user downloaded from MoSPI's PLFS dashboard (a one-page PDF, no embedded source URL). The dashboard has no public API or downloadable CSV, so this is a manually read, committed snapshot rather than a live fetch — same pattern as fuel-price-delhi.json.

worker_population_ratio_by_year.confidence: high — four clean, well-separated columns, monotonic trend, low extraction risk

labour_force_participation_rate_by_quart.confidence: high for 2022-2024 (smooth quarter-to-quarter change); LOW for the four 2025-26 quarters
labour_force_participation_rate_by_quart.confidence_note: Every quarter-to-quarter change from Jan-Mar 2022 through Oct-Dec 2024 is under 1 percentage point, consistent with how LFPR normally moves. The next value jumps from Person 50.4 to 55.0 and Female 25.2 to 33.4 in one step, and the source chart's own axis is also missing a 'Jan-Mar 2025' label between Oct-Dec 2024 and Apr-Jun 2025. This looks more like a column-alignment artifact from extracting a 16-column table out of a flattened PDF than a real one-quarter jump of that size. Treat the last four quarters as unverified until cross-checked against MoSPI's own PLFS bulletin.

employment_status_distribution_urban.confidence: high on the three values; moderate on which value belongs to which legend entry
employment_status_distribution_urban.confidence_note: The chart's legend order was 'regular wage/salaried employees, self employed, Casual labour' but did not visually bind each percentage to its legend entry. The mapping below follows PLFS's well-documented urban pattern (self-employment is consistently the largest urban segment; casual labour the smallest) rather than a directly read label pairing.
